name: Klook
tagline: Marketplace app for booking tours, attraction tickets, transport passes and local activities, mostly across Asia.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Klook has no subscription: you pay per booking and the platform takes a cut from operators.

verdictSummary: There is no software here to replace, only a supply chain. The value of Klook is that a few hundred thousand local operators have agreed to sell inventory through it, with live availability, redeemable QR vouchers, multi-currency payment and a refund process when the boat does not show up. An agent can build you a beautiful trip planner in an afternoon and it will contain zero bookable tickets. You would also be reimplementing payments, chargebacks and consumer travel law, which is not a one-shot. The closest honest build is a personal itinerary and wishlist tracker that you fill in by hand.
coreLoopDIY: A local itinerary planner where you save activities you found yourself, pin them to days on a trip, track cost and booking confirmation numbers, and see the day plan in order.
requirements: Local machine or a small VPS
Willingness to paste in every activity by hand
whatYouLose: Actual bookable inventory: thousands of operators with live availability and instant confirmation
Payment, currency handling, and someone to chase for a refund when the tour is cancelled
Scannable e-vouchers that the gate staff already recognise
Price comparison and reviews from people who did the thing last week
Customer support at 2am in a country where you do not speak the language
moatNotes: Supply side took a decade of on-the-ground sales teams signing up operators city by city. That is a headcount moat, not a code moat.
whyPeopleStillPay: You do not pay Klook a subscription, you pay it a margin for certainty. The alternative is emailing a tour operator in a language you do not read, wiring a deposit, and hoping. Klook's product is the guarantee that a QR code on your phone gets you onto the bus, plus a refund path if it does not. No self-hosted app produces that, because the thing being sold is not software.
notes: The itinerary UI is a weekend project; the inventory is not. The moat is a decade of feet-on-the-ground deals with local operators plus the trust that your voucher will actually scan.
prompt:
Build a local-only trip itinerary planner called "Daybook". This is a personal planning tool, NOT a booking platform: it never touches a payment or a supplier API.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/daybook.db, schema created on boot if missing.
- Server actions for all mutations. No external API calls, no auth, no telemetry, no analytics.

Data model:
- trip: id, name, destination, start_date, end_date, currency, notes.
- activity: id, trip_id, title, url, operator, category (tour | ticket | transport | food | other), price_amount, price_currency, duration_minutes, notes, status (wishlist | booked | done | cancelled), confirmation_code, voucher_file_path.
- slot: id, activity_id, day_date, start_time, end_time. An activity may have zero slots (still on the wishlist) or one.

Screens:
1. Trips list, create and edit a trip.
2. Trip board: two columns. Left is the wishlist (activities with no slot). Right is a day-by-day column stack from start_date to end_date. Drag an activity onto a day to create a slot, drag back to unschedule. Use dnd-kit.
3. Day view: activities in time order, gaps shown, a running total of planned spend in the trip currency.
4. Activity detail: all fields editable, plus a file upload that copies a PDF or image voucher into ./data/vouchers and stores the path. Render a link to open it.

Also include:
- A paste box on the trip page: paste a block of text, it creates one wishlist activity per non-empty line using the line as the title. Crude on purpose.
- Export a trip to a single Markdown file, day headings and bullet lines, written to ./exports.
- Warn in the UI when two slots on the same day overlap.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, live availability, price lookup, supplier integrations, payments, currency conversion rates, mobile app, push notifications, sharing.

Add a README with setup, and a seed script that creates one example three-day trip so the board is not empty on first run. Any config goes in .env.example, though a correct build needs no secrets.
